title: First commandment (CCC 2084–2141)
hookLine: faith, hope and love of God, and no superstition

cards: A phone lights up at 7 a.m. with a daily horoscope: avoid big decisions, the stars are not on your side. On a dashboard, a little charm swings from the mirror. In a drawer, the lucky socks from the playoff game.
None of it looks like religion. Maybe a joke, maybe a half-belief. The first commandment has something to say about all of that, and about a great deal more.

teach.b: Back in year one you met the Ten Commandments as a whole. Now the Catechism walks through them one at a time.
In Exodus, God speaks first about what he has done, in the Douay-Rheims: "I am the Lord thy God, who brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage."
Only then the command: "Thou shalt not have strange gods before me." Rescue first, then the rule. The Catechism reads it as a call to the three virtues aimed straight at God.
Faith: trusting God and what he has revealed.

teach.h: FAITH, HOPE AND LOVE OF GOD.
teach.b: Hope: expecting from him the help to love him and reach the life he promises. Charity: loving God above everything, for his own sake.

In the desert, Jesus answers the tempter with words the Catechism places here: "The Lord thy God shalt thou adore, and him only shalt thou serve." Adoration, prayer, sacrifice and promises kept to God all put him first.
Then it names what pushes God out of first place.
Idolatry: making a god of anything that isn't God, which can be power, pleasure, race, ancestors, the state, money.
Divination: horoscopes, astrology, palm reading, mediums, all trying to grab hold of the future instead of trusting it to God.

teach.h: SUPERSTITION: GOOD THINGS USED AS MAGIC.
teach.b: And superstition, described carefully: not only lucky charms, but treating even good religious practices as if they worked like magic, by their outward form alone. A medal, a novena, a candle are not the problem.
Thinking they force God's hand is. In this reading, the first commandment is a question of order: whatever sits first in a life is what that life serves.

how: Catholics learn the commandments in catechism and use them in an examination of conscience before confession; the first is kept through prayer, the Mass, and trusting God over luck and fortune-telling.

o: giving a tenth of your income to the Church
a promise to pray before every single meal
God first, with no idol, charm or horoscope

games.q: the first commandment — tap the pairs.
p: making a god of what isn't God

s: Catholic teaching says medals and candles are superstition
the Catechism names superstition as treating practices like magic, by their outward form alone; the objects themselves aren't the problem.
in Exodus, God speaks of rescuing his people before giving the command
I am the Lord thy God, who brought thee out of the land of Egypt: rescue first, then the rule.
the Catechism says idols can include money and power
anything put in God's place, it says: power, pleasure, the state, money.

games.q: you're Jesus in the desert. the tempter offers you all the kingdoms of the world if you'll fall down and adore him. what do you say?
o: take the kingdoms and do good with them.
the Lord thy God shalt thou adore, and him only shalt thou serve.
ask for time to think it over.
games.why: in Matthew 4 Jesus answers with the words the Catechism places under the first commandment: God alone is adored.

practice: If there's one, let a small habit you lean on for luck come to mind: a ritual before a game, a number you avoid, a chain message forwarded just in case.

Ask what it's really asking for, safety, control, a good outcome, and notice that wish underneath the habit. If you pray, hand the same wish to God directly; if not, simply set the habit down for today.

wordCard.voice: First commandment. Thou shalt not have strange gods before me: faith, hope and love aimed at God first, and no idol, fortune-telling or superstition in his place. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: 'I am', the first word God speaks in Exodus 20:2.

carryVoice: Your line: god first. The commandments start with a rescue, not a rule. Until tomorrow.
